messages.content:
Risk: Data Privacy
Description: Impacts due to leakage and unauthorized use, disclosure, or de-anonymization of biometric, health, location, or other personally identifiable information or sensitive data.
Concern: None
Policy: Clinical Staff Credentials & Institutional Data

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#T1597.001: Threat Intel Vendors — Adversaries may search private data from threat intelligence vendors for information that can be used during targeting. Threat intelligence vendors may offer paid feeds or portals that offer more data than what is publicly reported. Although sensitive details (such as customer names and other identifiers) may be redacted, this information may contain trends regarding breaches such as target industries, attribution claims, and successful TTPs/countermeasures.(Citation: D3Secutrity CTI Feeds) [found by 15/50 queries]
  Siblings: Purchase Technical Data
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0024.000: Infer Training Data Membership - ATLAS — Adversaries may infer the membership of a data sample or global characteristics of the data in its training set, which raises privacy concerns.
Some strategies make use of a shadow model that could be obtained via [Train Proxy via Replication](/techniques/AML.T0005.001), others use statistics of model prediction scores.

This can cause the victim model to leak private information, such as PII of those in the training set or other forms of protected IP. [found by 11/50 queries]
  Siblings: Extract AI Model - ATLAS, Invert AI Model - ATLAS
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0024: Exfiltration via AI Inference API - ATLAS — Adversaries may exfiltrate private information via [AI Model Inference API Access](/techniques/AML.T0040).
AI Models have been shown leak private information about their training data (e.g.  [Infer Training Data Membership](/techniques/AML.T0024.000), [Invert AI Model](/techniques/AML.T0024.001)).
The model itself may also be extracted ([Extract AI Model](/techniques/AML.T0024.002)) for the purposes of [AI Intellectual Property Theft](/techniques/AML.T0048.004).

Exfiltration of information relating to private training data raises privacy concerns.
Private training data may include personally identifiable information, or other protected data. [found by 10/50 queries]
  Siblings: LLM Response Rendering - ATLAS, Exfiltration via AI Agent Tool Invocation - ATLAS, LLM Data Leakage - ATLAS
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#HealthDataExposure: Health Data Exposure — Unauthorized disclosure of protected health information including medical records, diagnoses, treatments, or prescription histories. [found by 9/50 queries]
  Siblings: Unauthorized Surveillance, Direct Identifier Exposure, Employment Data Exposure
- http://d3fend.mitre.org/ontologies/d3fend.owl#AML.T0024.001: Invert AI Model - ATLAS — AI models' training data could be reconstructed by exploiting the confidence scores that are available via an inference API.
By querying the inference API strategically, adversaries can back out potentially private information embedded within the training data.
This could lead to privacy violations if the attacker can reconstruct the data of sensitive features used in the algorithm. [found by 9/50 queries]
  Siblings: Extract AI Model - ATLAS, Infer Training Data Membership - ATLAS

axes.rationale: This technique involves using AI models to infer membership of data samples, which directly relates to the risk of data privacy breaches by potentially exposing sensitive information.

axes.cco_class_label: Exfiltration via AI Inference API - ATLAS
axes.rationale: This technique involves exfiltrating private information via AI inference APIs, which is a direct method of data privacy violation.
This class represents the unauthorized disclosure of protected health information, which is a core concern in data privacy risks.
